story_title: Trading Strategy Performance in 2009 Market Volatility
story_subtitle: Analyzing short, long, and neutral signals across price movements and returns during June-July 2009

story_pieces.narration: Short signals consistently outperformed long signals with an average return of -2.3% versus 2.1%, though neutral signals had no impact on returns.
story_pieces.question: Which trading strategy (short/long/neutral) delivered better average returns during this period?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (strategy type vs. average return)

story_pieces.narration: The single highest return of 15.49% occurred on June 22nd when the market surged from $30.40 to $31.17 despite a 'short' signal.
story_pieces.question: Which date had the highest single-day return, and how did it contrast with the trading signal?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (date vs. close price) with highlight marker

story_pieces.narration: The worst performing day with a -10.42% return happened on June 24th, when the market dropped from $30.58 to $29.05 after a 'long' signal.
story_pieces.question: Which date had the most significant negative return, and how did it contrast with the trading signal?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (date vs. close price) with highlight marker

story_pieces.narration: Short signals were triggered 18 times (60% of total signals) while long signals occurred 10 times (33%), with only one neutral signal recorded.
story_pieces.question: How did the frequency of trading signals (short/long/neutral) compare during this period?
story_pieces.visualization: stacked bar chart (signal type vs. count) with percentage labels

story_pieces.narration: The market showed a strong upward trend from June 15th to July 2nd, with cumulative returns of 34.9% despite mixed signal patterns.
story_pieces.question: How did the overall market trend correlate with the distribution of trading signals?
story_pieces.visualization: area chart (date vs. close price) with overlaid signal indicators
